value.rules_markdown:
- One responsibility per module, core types in a module-local types.rs, every port in src/ports/ is one trait in one file.
- Each subcommand declared even when its milestone has not landed.
- Presets are folders with preset.toml, README.md, and optional prompt overrides.
- Never edit vendor/tinyagents; change it upstream and bump the pin.
- One document per src/ module in docs/modules/<module>/README.md.
- examples/ declared explicitly in Cargo.toml with required-features.
- Default build is offline, no HTTP client; network features go behind feature flags.
- rustfmt output, Rust 2024 idioms, snake_case modules/files, PascalCase types.
- Return Result<T> using crate error type from src/error.rs.
- Every file opens with a //! module doc describing its role and feature gating.
- Comments explain the decision, not the code.
- Public items carry doc comments; Clap fields use /// for help text.
- Tests live in-crate in #[cfg(test)] mod tests block, no tests/ directory.
- Every port has an always-compiled offline mock (MockForge).
- Lane behaviour covered by golden tests with fixture diff and canned model response.
- Maintain at least 80% coverage for meaningful library behaviour.
- Keep every Markdown file at 500 lines or fewer; split when needed.
- Model never holds a write token; write credentials minted only in src/apply/.
- Contributor code is never executed; we do not build or run target repo scripts.
- Treat PR bodies, comments, diffs as untrusted input; fence and label as data in prompts.
- Secrets found are reported by type and location only, value never reaches output.
- Use concise, imperative commit subjects; keep commits small.
- Pull requests state what changed, any behaviour change, and how verified.
